summary:
Central Visayas stands under the national framework of the Republic of the Philippines. Within the region, protection against discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity is set at the municipal level rather than by a regional instrument. In July 2024 Mandaue City signed the implementing rules and regulations of its Anti-Discrimination Ordinance, at a signing held with the city mayor, the KAABAG LGBT Federation and the United Nations Development Programme.

A town in northern Cebu passed a Comprehensive Anti-Discrimination Ordinance days before the end of Pride Month, safeguarding against discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity. The source does not identify the town, the year, or the exact date of passage.
tangentialFactors:
The two documented instruments are municipal, so the protection a trans visitor can point to in Central Visayas depends on which city or municipality they are in. The inventory does not establish how many other localities in the region have comparable ordinances.

Both measures were adopted with visible local political backing: the Mandaue City signing was held with the city mayor and a local LGBT federation, and the northern Cebu ordinance was passed at the close of Pride Month.
localsOnly: Residents of Mandaue City have had the implementing rules of the city's Anti-Discrimination Ordinance in force since July 2024, adopted by the city government alongside the KAABAG LGBT Federation. Residents of the northern Cebu town covered by the Comprehensive Anti-Discrimination Ordinance have a municipal instrument against sexual orientation and gender identity discrimination. Neither source describes complaint procedures, penalties or enforcement outcomes.
outOfScopeNotes:
The town in northern Cebu and the date of its ordinance are not identified in the source, and the year of passage is not stated. Whether either ordinance covers employment, housing, public accommodations, or visitors as distinct from residents is not described.

No record specific to Central Visayas of complaints, enforcement action or violence against trans people appears in the source inventory, and no regional-level SOGI statute is documented.
